title: Section 92 — Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide

content.overview: BNS s. 92 — Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide. BNS restatement of IPC 316. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 316. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 92 is the rule on “Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide”. The section provides that whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 92 exists so that “Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
92. Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever does any act under such circumstances, that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, knowing that he is likely to cause the death of a pregnant woman, does an act which, if it caused the death of the woman, would amount to culpable homicide. The woman is injured, but does not die; but the death of an unborn quick child with which she is pregnant is thereby caused. A is guilty of the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 92 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). Of offences against child

learningObjectives: Master the elements of causing the death of a quick unborn child by an act that would amount to culpable homicide if the mother had died.
Understand the legal status of an unborn child quick in the womb and the transfer/application of homicide-grade blameworthiness.
Examine statutory illustrations and the punishment of imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 92 provides that whoever does any act under such circumstances that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Applies homicide-grade culpability to the killing of a quick unborn child when an act intended to harm or kill the mother results in the death of the unborn child.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 92 (corresponding to IPC s. 316).
Threshold condition: Act done under circumstances that if death of the mother were caused, it would amount to culpable homicide.
Result: The act causes the death of a quick unborn child (while the mother survives or suffers injury).
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to ten years, and fine.

Statutory illustration: A, knowing he is likely to cause the death of a pregnant woman, does an act which would amount to culpable homicide if she died. She is injured but survives; the quick unborn child dies. A is guilty under this section.
essentialIngredients: The woman was pregnant with a quick unborn child.
The accused did an act capable of causing death.
The act was done under circumstances that if the woman had died, the accused would be guilty of culpable homicide.
The act caused the death of the quick unborn child.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 92 addresses a specific tragedy: a violent assault directed against a pregnant woman carrying a quick child (where fetal life has progressed to perceptible movement), where the act has the gravity of culpable homicide. If the mother dies, the accused is tried for culpable homicide or murder. However, if the mother survives the attack but the quick unborn child dies in the womb as a direct consequence of the injuries, Section 92 applies. The law tests the accused's liability by asking: 'If the mother had died from this act, would the accused be guilty of culpable homicide?' If yes, that culpable mental state sustains liability under Section 92 for destroying the quick unborn child, punishable with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
examples: Teaching example (Assault on pregnant woman causing fetal death): An assailant brutally beats a heavily pregnant woman with an iron rod, aiming at her vital organs. Bystanders intervene and medical treatment saves the woman's life, but the violent trauma causes placental abruption and kills the eight-month quick unborn child. The assailant is guilty under s. 92.

Teaching example (Accidental collision): A driver negligently causes a traffic collision resulting in minor injuries to a pregnant woman and subsequent miscarriage. Since simple negligence does not amount to culpable homicide, s. 92 is not attracted (though other traffic and negligence provisions apply).
distinctions: Section 92 vs Section 91: Section 91 requires a specific intention directed at the child to prevent live birth; Section 92 requires an act that would amount to culpable homicide against the mother.
Section 92 vs Section 88: Section 88 penalizes causing miscarriage generally; Section 92 requires the severe culpability threshold of culpable homicide directed towards the mother.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who shot at a pregnant woman with intent to kill her, missing her heart but striking her abdomen and killing her quick unborn child while she survived, is guilty under s. 92.
Rule: If the act would have amounted to culpable homicide/murder had the woman died, causing the death of a quick unborn child satisfies BNS s. 92.
Application: Shooting at vital organs constitutes an act amounting to culpable homicide; the mother survived, but the quick child died.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 92.
